title: Humphrey's own recording session
summary: He recalls making a record but not the titles, and being asked to play again after construction work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Tell me about the recording you made, as I was to make. Do you remember that?
Yeah, I remember making a record, but I can't remember the name of the pieces.
I really, I don't, I've only heard those records once or twice, eh?

I have, uh, I have, uh, the fact I had one, I went to somebody around here, because I haven't got a clear. I've forgotten now who I learned it to. Yeah. A fellow and, uh, the doctor, you know, and Virginia gave me the record, you know, a small, a small album. Yeah. And, uh, did you rehearse for that session? No. I hadn't paid in about a month when the nurse came to me.
I just put, put the horn up doing construction work. And they come by and asked me.

And, you know, just run over my horn again. But I came, well, the work was scarce then, and I wasn't, with no organized bands. So I went on doing construction work. And they come by and asked me. And, you know, just run over my horn again. But I came, well, the work was scarce then, and I wasn't, with no organized bands. So I went on doing construction work.
Now that was in 1926 when you made it. That was 26. Remember you said the other day it was 26 with Buddy?
Yeah, 26 or 27. I, you know, I can't, can't think of the dates. Yeah.
So now, when you were playing with Buddy then, that was before when you made it. Yeah.
Yeah, before then. Because I went off on the road that night. Yeah. I'd gone down to Crowley, Louisiana, playing with the Black Eagle, playing.
